Goal: 1-week deload (week 5) for an advanced 26 y.o. male coming off 4 weeks high-volume hypertrophy (≈18 working sets/session, compounds at RPE 8.5). Use the same exercises but reduce volume and intensity to promote recovery while maintaining movement pattern and neuromuscular stimulus.

Deload principles applied
- Volume: reduce weekly and per-session working sets to ~40–60% of normal (target ~8–10 working sets/session instead of 18).
- Intensity: reduce load to ~60–70% of usual working loads (RPE ~5–6). Avoid training to failure.
- Maintain frequency and exercise selection (same exercises) but shorten sessions.
- Preserve technique, mobility, light acceleration work and brief activation rounds.
- Emphasize sleep, nutrition (maintain calories or small reduction if body-fat loss desired), hydration and mobility/soft-tissue work.

Weekly format (single-week deload)
Assumptions about the client’s typical split: I’ll mirror the same exercise selection each session you’ve been using (compound focus). If your prior program was an upper/lower/upper/lower or push/pull/legs, use the same days — below I present 4 sessions (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B). If your client normally trains 4x per week, use this. If they trained 5–6x, they can skip one or convert extra sessions to active recovery.

Session structure (apply to each session)
- Warm-up (10–12 min): general cardio 5 min easy (bike/row), joint mobility, 1–2 warm-up sets per main compound at ~50–60% of the working set load.
- Main work: keep same exercises; do 40–60% of usual sets, and reduce intensity to RPE 5–6. All sets stop well short of failure.
- Ancillary work: reduce sets to 1–2 sets each, light, aiming for movement quality not fatigue.
- Mobility / breathing / soft tissue: 8–10 min at end.

How to scale loads: If typical compounds were RPE 8.5 loads, reduce to ~60–70% of that load or choose a weight that feels ~RPE 5–6 for the prescribed reps. Example: if you normally do 100 kg for 6 at RPE 8.5, deload to ~60–70 kg for 6 at ~RPE 5–6.

Deload week plan (4 sessions). Keep exercise names exactly as your usual; below I provide an example mapping to common exercises. Replace with the exact variants you use if different.

Day 1 — Upper A
Warm-up: 5 min bike + thoracic mobility, band pull-aparts, shoulder dislocations. 2 warm-up sets for bench and row.
1) Barbell Bench Press — 3 sets x 5–6 reps @ RPE 5–6 (≈60–70% usual working load). Pause warm-up sets 8–10 reps at light loads as needed.
2) Bent-Over Barbell Row (or Pendlay row) — 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 5–6.
3) Overhead Press (standing) — 2 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 5–6.
4) Lat Pulldown or Chin-up (assisted/light) — 2 sets x 8–10 reps @ easy tempo.
5) Dumbbell Lateral Raise — 1 set x 12–15 reps (light, focus on control).
6) Biceps curl (barbell or dumbbell) — 1 set x 10–12 reps (light).
Cool-down: 8–10 min mobility/soft-tissue for pecs/shoulders. Breathing work.

Day 2 — Lower A
Warm-up: 5–8 min row/ bike + dynamic hip mobility, 2 light warm-up sets for squats/deadlifts.
1) Barbell Back Squat (or variant you normally use) — 3 sets x 5 reps @ RPE 5–6 (≈60–70% load).
2) Romanian Deadlift (RDL) or Stiff-Leg — 2 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 5–6 (light, hinge pattern).
3) Leg Press or Front Squat (whichever you usually do as accessory) — 2 sets x 8 reps @ easy.
4) Walking Lunges or Bulgarian Split Squat — 1 set x 8–10 reps per leg (light).
5) Calf raise (standing/seated) — 1 set x 12–15 reps (light).
Core: 1 set planks 45–60s or dead-bugs 1 x 12/side.
Cool-down: 8–10 min foam roll quads/hips + hip flexor stretching.

Day 3 — Upper B
Warm-up: same structure.
1) Incline DB Bench Press (or your usual incline) — 3 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 5–6.
2) Single-Arm Dumbbell Row or Seated Cable Row — 3 sets x 6–8 reps @ light.
3) Pull-up (assisted if needed) — 2 sets x 6–8 reps (controlled).
4) Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press or Arnold Press — 2 sets x 6 reps @ easy.
5) Face Pulls — 1 set x 15 reps (band/cable).
6) Triceps pushdown or overhead triceps extension — 1 set x 12 reps (light).
Cool-down: mobility + breathing.

Day 4 — Lower B
Warm-up: same.
1) Deadlift (conventional or sumo; same variant used in prior block) — 3 sets x 3–4 reps @ RPE 5–6 (note lower rep range for CNS unloading; keep weight light).
2) Front Squat, Goblet Squat, or Safety-Bar Squat (your usual accessory) — 2 sets x 6 reps @ easy.
3) Glute Bridge or Hip Thrust (light) — 2 sets x 8–10 reps @ RPE 5–6.
4) Hamstring curl (lying or seated) — 1 set x 10–12 reps (light).
5) Calf raise — 1 set x 12–15 reps.
Core: Pallof press 1 x 10/side.
Cool-down: foam roll + mobility.

Notes on set/rep philosophy and what to cut
- Reduce per-exercise sets: typical compounds that were 4–5 sets now 2–3 sets. Accessories that were 3–4 sets become 1–2 sets.
- Keep tempo controlled, avoid extended eccentrics that produce high soreness. Use normal 2-1-2 tempo, avoid slow negatives.
- Keep rest periods moderate; you can slightly shorten rest to keep session length down but avoid metabolic stress. Rest 90–180s for compounds, 60–90s for accessories.
- No AMRAPs, no drop sets, no rest-pause.

Active recovery / optional extra
- On 1–2 off days do 20–30 min low-intensity cardio (walk, bike), mobility session or yoga. Avoid heavy conditioning.
- If client trains 5–6x/week normally, convert the extra sessions into 20–30 min mobility/skill or skip them.

Nutrition and recovery guidance (for the week)
- Calories: maintain approx maintenance intake. If the goal is recovery and maintain body comp, keep calories steady. Small deficit ok only if conscious of potential recovery trade-offs.
- Protein: keep high to support muscle repair: ~2.0–2.4 g/kg/day (for 26 y.o. male advanced lifter).
- Carbs: moderate — align with workout timing; pre/post meals with adequate carbs to support training quality.
- Fats: ~20–30% of calories.
- Sodium & fluids: maintain normal intake, hydrate well.
- Sleep: prioritize 8+ hours/night; reduce late-night stressors.
- Supplements (if used): continue creatine, fish oil, multivitamin; caffeine limited if interfering with sleep.
- Recovery modalities: daily mobility, 2–3 short soft-tissue sessions, contrast showers optional. Avoid deep tissue sessions immediately before heavy sessions if they cause soreness.

Monitoring and readiness for next block
- Track RPE and subjective recovery. Aim for session RPE ~5–6 and little to no soreness returning across the week.
- If client still feels fatigued at end of week, consider extending deload by another 3–4 days with continued low volume/intensity.
- Begin next intensification block after this week. On Day 1 of the next block, use slightly lower loads than pre-deload for the first session to re-assess (e.g., 80–85% of pre-deload working loads) and monitor bar speed.

- Tuesday: Lower A
- Wednesday: Active recovery / mobility
- Thursday: Upper B
- Friday: Lower B
- Saturday: Light cardio / mobility or rest
- Sunday: Rest

- Protocol: 2 sets × 2 reps at 40–50% 1RM (or standard deload load for that exercise). Rest 2–3 minutes between sets. Record average and peak velocity.
- Interpretation: 5–10% drop in velocity vs prior baseline indicates freshness/fatigue.

2) Heavy-ish single at RPE 7 (not a max)
- Why: gives a snapshot of strength without CNS disruption.
- How: choose one key compound (deadlift or squat) and after warm-up do one intentional single at an estimated RPE 7 (i.e., 3 reps in reserve). Do only one such single. If you want bilateral comparison, choose deadlift; if you want lower body but less CNS stress, use a heavy single squat at RPE 7.
- Protocol: after warm-ups, load a weight that feels like RPE 7 and perform 1 controlled rep. Record weight and perceived RPE.
- Safety: stop if technique deteriorates or pain occurs. Do not follow with more heavy sets.

3) Bar speed on an upper-body push (neutral-grip DB floor press)
- Why: since bench was swapped, test pressing speed and control.
- How: 2 sets × 2 reps at a light-to-moderate DB load (roughly the deload working weight or ~40–50% of usual bench 1RM). Measure concentric peak velocity or subjective bar speed on a 1–10 scale.
- Protocol: same rest 2–3 minutes. Record results.

4) Vertical jump or broad jump (optional)
- Why: unloaded neuromuscular marker for lower-body power that’s low-fatigue if done correctly.
- How: perform 2 maximal vertical jumps (or 2 broad jumps) with full recovery (90–120s). Record best of 2. Avoid if any soreness or back issues.
- Note: keep only 1–2 maximal attempts to avoid fatigue.

5) Isometric mid-thigh pull or isometric squat (if equipment available)
- Why: high correlation to dynamic strength, very low fatigue if kept to 1–2 brief maximal pulls (~3–5s).
- How: 1–2 maximal 3–5s pulls with 3–4 minutes rest. Record peak force if you have a force plate or rig.
- Safety: maintain technique and keep attempts minimal.

- Why: simple, no extra testing equipment needed.
- How: during a deload working set (e.g., first set of back squat at 3×5), note the RPE. Alternatively, perform a single AMRAP is not recommended. Track RPE and bar speed instead.

Deload week summary (Week 5) — overview for advanced 26 y.o. male after 4-week high-volume hypertrophy block

Week intent
- Maintain movement patterns and neuromuscular stimulus while prioritizing recovery.
- Reduce volume to roughly 40–60% of prior sessions and drop intensity to submaximal efforts, except two planned moderate bumps (Wed & Fri) kept controlled.
- Keep same exercises with bench swapped for neutral-grip DB floor/incline presses to protect a cranky shoulder.

Weekly layout (days)
- Monday: Upper A (deload)
- Tuesday: Lower A (deload)
- Wednesday: Speed/power upper + mobility (controlled bump)
- Thursday: Upper B (deload)
- Friday: Slightly bumped Lower B (controlled heavier work)
- Saturday: Zone 2 cardio 30 min (or active recovery)
- Sunday: Rest

Per-session content and working-set counts (this week vs last week)
Assumption: last week ≈ 18 working sets per session (high-volume hypertrophy, compounds ~RPE 8.5). Targets below reduce sets to ~8–9 per session on planned deload days; Wednesday/Friday are slightly bumped but still well below prior volume.

Monday — Upper A
- This week: 9 working sets
  - Neutral-grip DB floor press 3×6
  - Bent-over barbell row 3×6
  - Standing OHP 1×6
  - Lat pulldown / light chin-up 1×8–10
  - Face pulls 1×12–15
- Last week (typical): ~18 working sets (e.g., bench 4–5×6, rows 4×8, OHP 3×8, lat work 3×8–10, accessories multiple sets)
- Volume change: ~50% reduction in working sets (~18 → 9)
- Intensity change: RPE ~8.5 → RPE 5–6 (stop well short of failure)

Tuesday — Lower A
- This week: 8 working sets (+1 core)
  - Back squat 3×5
  - Romanian deadlift 2×6
  - Leg press/front squat 2×8
  - Walking lunges/Bulgarian split 1×8–10/leg
- Last week: ~18 working sets (higher sets per lift, more accessory volume)
- Volume change: ~55–60% reduction
- Intensity change: RPE ~8.5 → RPE 5–6

Wednesday — Speed/Power Upper + Mobility (controlled bump)
- This week: short speed block + mobility; ~6–8 short high-intent sets but low load
  - Neutral-grip DB speed press 4×3 @ ~40–50% 1RM (bar speed focus)
  - 2×3 vertical/broad jumps (optional)
  - 2×15 face pulls / band work
  - 20 min mobility
  - Zone 2 optional (shortened to 20–25 min if used)
- Last week: mobility and cardio not typical as heavy training day
- Volume change: fewer working sets than a normal high-volume upper session but slightly more neuromuscular stimulus than a strict deload upper
- Intensity change: intent/velocity high but absolute load low; perceived RPE on speed sets ~4–6, with one or two controlled sets possibly up to ~6.5–7 for stimulation only

Thursday — Upper B
- This week: 9 working sets
  - Incline neutral-grip DB press 3×6
  - Single-arm DB row / seated cable row 3×6–8
  - Pull-up 1×6–8
  - Seated neutral-grip DB press 1×6
  - Triceps 1×12
- Last week: ~18 working sets
- Volume change: ~50% reduction
- Intensity change: RPE ~8.5 → RPE 5–6

Friday — Slightly bumped Lower B
- This week: ~9–10 working sets but with one controlled heavier block
  - Deadlift 2×3 @ RPE ~6.5–7 (controlled, 2 sets only)
  - Front/goblet squat 2×5–6
  - Hip thrust 2×8–10
  - Hamstring curl 1×10–12
  - Core: Pallof 1×10/side
  - Optional light explosive assistance (kettlebell swings/med-ball slams) 2×5
- Last week: ~18 working sets with higher deadlift/squat volume
- Volume change: overall set count down ~40–55%, but Wednesday/Friday bumps provide slightly higher neuromuscular load than pure deload—still substantially less than last week
- Intensity change: most work RPE 5–6, with deadlift top sets at RPE ~6.5–7 (submaximal, not a 1RM attempt)

Saturday — Zone 2 Cardio
- This week: 30 min Zone 2 (low intensity)
- Last week: likely no extra cardio or different conditioning
- Purpose: maintain aerobic base, aid recovery

Sunday — Rest

Overall week comparison vs last week
- Volume: per-session working sets reduced from ~18 → generally 8–9 on Monday/Tuesday/Thursday; Wednesday/Friday provide extra stimulus but total weekly per-session sets remain ~40–60% of the prior week. Net weekly volume is roughly half (or less) of the previous hypertrophy week.
- Intensity: compounds dropped from RPE ~8.5 across the block to RPE ~5–6 on most sets. Two bumped sessions include short sets at RPE ~6.5–7 (Wednesday speed intent and Friday deadlift singles/doubles) but nothing near true maximal effort (no RPE 8.5–9+ sets, no AMRAPs, no 1RMs).
- Fatigue/CNS: Designed to reduce peripheral and central fatigue while letting the client feel stimulated. Wednesday/Friday bumps increase neuromuscular freshness without reversing the deload benefits because they are limited in set count and kept submaximal.
- Shoulder protection: bench replaced with neutral-grip DB floor/incline presses to reduce shoulder irritation; mobility and banded rotator work included midweek and daily as cool-downs.

Practical notes
- Walk weights down to ~60–70% of last-week working loads for most sets, or pick loads that correspond to RPE 5–6. For the Wednesday speed work use ~40–50% 1RM for ballistic intent. For the Friday deadlift block select a weight that is challenging but leaves ~3 reps in reserve (RPE ~6.5–7).
- Keep rest between compound sets long (2.5–4 min for heavier/submax work) and accessory rest ~60–90s.
- Maintain calories at maintenance, protein ~2.0–2.4 g/kg, prioritize sleep 8+ hrs.
- Monitor soreness, sleep, morning HR and RPE. If fatigue accumulates, revert Wednesday/Friday to the original low-intensity deload plan.
